2. It has been alleged, amongst other, in the petition that the Respondent No. 1 is the wife of the Petitioner. The Respondent No. 2 is the City Bank Limited, a scheduled commercial bank incorporated and regulated under the Bank Companies Act 1991. The Pro-forma Respondent No. 3 is the Dhaka Stock Exchange ("DSE"). The Pro-forma Respondent No. 4 is Pubali Bank Limited ("PBL"). The Pro-forma Respondent No. 5 is the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms. The Pro-forma Respondent No. 6 is Al-Arafah Islami Bank Limited. The addresses of the Respondents and Pro-forma Respondents are stated in the cause title. The Petitioner has no cause of action against the Pro-forma Respondents and they are impleaded herein for the purpose of giving a complete account of the events that have given rise to the instant application under section 43 of the Companies Act 1994 ("the Act"); that the Petitioner was the holder of 34,555,152 ordinary shares of the Respondent No. 2 Bank. These shares were held by the Petitioner under a Beneficiary Owner Account (BO Account) bearing reference No. 1203440019185096 maintained with PBL (the Pro-forma Respondent No. 4). A true copy of the share balance of the Petitioner as on 7-5-2014 under BO Account No. 1203440019185096 maintained with PBL (Annexure A); that due to medical reasons, for the past 6 years, the Petitioner has been predominantly residing in London, UK and made infrequent trips to Bangladesh. Moreover, there has been matrimonial discord between the Petitioner and the Respondent No. 1 during this period. Taking advantage of the Petitioner's absence and with mala fide intention, the Respondent No. 1 forged and falsified documents, and out of the total 34,555,152 shares of the Petitioner, obtained transfer of the 2,77,00,000 (two crore seventy seven lac) shares (the Shares) ((more specifically described in the schedule herein below)) in her name under a Beneficiary Owner Account (BO Account) bearing reference No. 1203440019174870 maintained with PBL (the Pro-forma respondent No. 4); the Respondent No. 1 has forged and falsified in connection with the illegal transfer of the Shares, the Dematerialized Request Form (DRF) for share certificate Nos. 000476, 000477, 000478, 000479, 004733, 008852, 008853, 008854, 008855, 027091, 027092, 027093, 027094, 027095, 027096, 027097, 027098, 027099, 027100, 027101, 027102, 027103, 027104, 027105, 027224, 000048, 000049, 000050, 000163, 000164, 000165, 000166, 000167, 000168, 000169, 000170, 000171, 000172, 000248, 000249, 000250, 000346, 000347, 000348, 000470, 000471, 000472, 000473, 000474, 000475, 029404, 46166, 46334, 48611, 50268, 000440, 000441, 000442, 000467, 000448, 000450, 000451, 004563, 004564, 004565, 004566, 004567, 004568, 004569, 004570, 004571, 004572, 004573, 004574, 004576, 004577, 004578, 004579, 004580, 004581, 004582, 004583, 004584, 004585, 004586, 004587, 004588, 004589, 004590, 004591, 004592, 004916, 027063, 027064, 027065, 027066, 027067, 027068, 027069, 027070, 027071, 027072, 027073, 027074, 027075, 027076, 027077, 027078, 46164, 46332, 48609, 50266, 000153, 000154, 000155, 000156, 000157, 000158, 000159, 000160, 000161, 000162, 000457, 000460, 004731, 004732, 004917, 004918, 004919, 004920, 004921, 004922, 004923, 004924, 004925, 004926, 004927, 027079, 027080, 027081, 027082, 027083, 027084, 027085, 027086, 027087, 027088, 027089, 027090, 027223, 029403, 46165, 46333 and 48610 ("the DRF Forms") Annexure: B Series; that application in Form II1(A) under regulation 42 of the Listing Regulation dated 7-5-2014 (received by DSE on 8-5-2014) for approval of the gifting of listed shares outside the trading system of the stock exchange ("the Gift Application") Annexure C; that by a letter dated 12-5-2014 under reference No. DSE/ Listing/512 /2014 /3828, the Pro-forma Respondent No. 3 (DSE) informed the Petitioner that the proposed transfer of the Shares under the Gift Application was approved and the Petitioner was asked to deposit Taka 240,990 as service charge in favour of DSE (Annexure D); that by pay-order dated 19-5-2014 ("the DSE Pay Order") from the account of Noorani Flour Mills Ltd maintained with Bank Asia Limited (Tejgaon Link Road branch), DSE was paid Taka 240,990 service charge for approving the transfer of the Shares in the name of the Respondent No. 1 Annexure E; that by a letter dated 20-5-2014, PBL notified the Petitioner that under Transfer Sequence No. 45731369 ("the PBL Transfer Sequence Number") the purported request for transfer or change of ownership of the Shares in the name of the Respondent No. 1 was setup. A true copy of the PBL Transfer Sequence Number contained in the letter dated 20-5-2014 Annexure F; that by a letter dated 29-5-2014 of the Petitioner ("the Forged Letter"), DSE was informed that the Shares have been transferred from the Petitioner to the Respondent No. 1 as per the PBL Transfer Sequence Number. It is emphatically stated that the signature appearing in the Forged Letter is falsified Annexure G; that it is submitted that the transfer of the Shares from the Petitioner to the Respondent No. 1 has been completed through forgery and fraudulent means and is void in the eye of the law because: 

 4. The respondent No. 1 has filed affidavit-in-opposition denying all material allegations stating that the statements made in paragraph No. 3 of the said application, the petitioner admits that he was holder of 3,45,55,152 ordinary shares of the respondent No. 2 bank and the said 3,45,55,152 ordinary shares includes the said 60,46,540 shares in respect of which the petitioner alleged that DRFs were forged. When the petitioner admits the ownership of the said dematerialized shares including the said 60,46,540 freshly dematerialized shares, the petitioner cannot alleged that the dematerialization of the said 60,46,540 shares was done by way of forgery; that the statements made in paragraph No. 4 of the said application are false and hence denied. The respondent No. 1 did not forge any document whatsoever. The petitioner himself through his employees transferred the said shares in the name of the respondent No. 1. Now at this stage the petitioner cannot challenge the said transfer of shares in the name of the respondent No. 1; that the statements made in the paragraph Nos. 5, 6 and 7 are matters of record; that the statements made in paragraph Nos. 8 and 9 are false and hence, denied for the reasons stated hereinabove in the instant affidavit-in-opposition; that the statements made in paragraph Nos. 10,11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 are also false and hence, denied. The respondent No. 1 has also stated a positive case, in paragraph No. 2, in which she has stated, amongst other, that the petitioner submitted a share balance dated 7-5-2014 before this court (Annexure-"A"). This share balance was issued by Pubali Bank Securities Ltd. on 7-5-2014. This share balance dated 7-5-2014 shows the then current balance of shares as 3,45,55,152 which includes the said freshly dematerialized 60,46,540 shares. This share balance is a very crucial document, which shows that the falsity of the petitioner's claims. The said share balance document was issued after dematerialization and was issued in the year 2014. Therefore, the petitioner himself collected the said share balance document in the year 2014 just immediately after dematerialization of the said 60,46,540 shares. Therefore, the fact that he collected the said share balance document on 7-5-2014, and preserved the said document for more than three years, categorically proves that the petitioner himself knew the said dematerialization and he had direct connection to get the said 60,46,540 shares dematerialized; that the petitioner has further alleged that he did not sign application for approval of gifting of shares dated 7-5-2014 (Annexure-C). The petitioner also alleged that the respondent No. 1 forged the said application for approval of gifting the shares dated 7-5-2014. On the very day of 7-5-2014, the respondent No. 1 was not in Bangladesh. Therefore, there is no scope for the respondent No. 1 to forge and submit the said application for approval to gifting on 7-5-2014 to Dhaka Stock Exchange Ltd. Further, the very date of the said application for approval of the gifting of shares submitted with Dhaka Stock Exchange Ltd. coincides with the very date of obtaining share balance document obtained from Pubali Bank Securities Ltd. Therefore, the person who obtained the share balance document dated 7-5-2014 (Annexure-A) must have submitted the said application for approval to the gifting of shares. It is stated herein by the respondent No. 1 that the employees of the petitioner at the instruction of the petitioner obtained the said share balance document dated 7-5-2014 and submitted the said application for approval to the gifting dated 7-5-2014; that From the letter No. DSE/ Listing/512/2014/3828 dated 12-5-2014 (Annexure-D) issued by Dhaka Stock Exchange Ltd., it appears that Dhaka Stock Exchange Ltd. directed the petitioner to pay Taka 2,40,990 in favour of Dhaka Stock Exchange Ltd. on account of transfer of the said 2,77,00,000 share from BO Account of the petitioner to the BO Account of respondent No. 1. The petitioner disowns the acceptance and knowledge of the said letter dated 12-5-2014. But petitioner not only knew the existence and contents of the said letter dated 12-5-2014, but the petitioner also directed one employee of the petitioner, namely, one Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan to arrange payment of the share transfer fees of Tk. 2,40,990. The said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan on 21-5-2014 issued a note in favour of CEO, Mr Moniruzzaman and Ms. Rabeya Sultana putting details instructions given by Mr Zakaria, i.e., the petitioner over phone. Therefore, it is clear that the petitioner directed the said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan to do all the relevant acts for transferring the said shares from BO Account of the petitioner to the BO Account of the respondent No. 1. Hence, the petitioner being involved directly in transferring the said shares from BO Account of the petitioner to the BO Account of the respondent No. 1, he at this stage cannot challenge the same, when for such transfer the transferee cannot be involved, neither the transferee has any role in any procedure for such transfer of dematerialized shares. The petitioner simply informed the respondent No. 1 that he gifted the said 2,77,00,000 shares in her favour, which she merrily and gladly accepted. The CEO referred to in the said note dated 21-5-2014 of the said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan is Mr Harunur Rashid, who made some hand writing comments on the said note issued by Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan. The said Harunur Rashid shall give deposition, if this Hon'ble Court so directs. In the said note the said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan his telephonic conversation with the petitioner and also confirmed that the petitioner on 20-5-2014 consented the payment of share transfer fees. This Court may also be pleased to issue summons upon the said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan, who is an employee of the petitioner. Copy of the said note dated 21-5-2014 (ANNEXURE-2). The original of the said note is under custody of the said Mr Harunur Rashid; that the petitioner arranged payment of the said share transfer fees of Taka 2,40,990 to Dhaka Stock Exchange Ltd. by way of Pay Order through his employees, photocopy of which the petitioner has annexed as Annexure-E. One Mr Moniruzzaman applied to Bank Asia Ltd. for obtaining a pay order of Taka 2,40,990 only with the view to deposit the said pay order as share transfer fees with Dhaka Stock Exchange against the transfer of the said 2,77,00,000 shares from BO account of the petitioner to the BO account of the respondent No. 1. The signature of the said Moniruzzaman is conspicuous as the signature of the applicant in the said pay order application dated 19-5-2014. The original of the said pay order application form is lying with the Bank Asia Ltd., Tejgaon Link Road Branch. On this material date, i.e.19-5-2014, the respondent No. 1 was not in the country. The petitioner having instructed the said Shamsul Alam Bhuyian and the said Moniruzzaman arranged the said pay order of Taka 2,40,990 to be deposited with DSE. The said Moniruzzaman is a henchman of the petitioner. The respondent No. 1, in a separate incident, had to lodge an ejahar dated 15-2-2017, (which was registered as Chalkbazar Model Police Station Case No. 20 dated 15-2-2017) against, amongst other, the said Moniruzzaman for the offence of assaulting employees of the respondent No. 1 at the dictate of the petitioner. The said Moniruzzaman and the said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan paid the said amount of Taka 2,40,990at the instruction of the petitioner. Therefore, the petitioner is well aware of the transfer of the said shares from BO Account of petitioner to the BO Account of respondent No. 1 and most importantly the petitioner was personally active and involved in transferring the said shares from BO Account of the petitioner to the BO Account of the respondent No. 1. (Annexure-3 & 4); that it is clear that the said Moniruzzaman obtained pay order dated 19-5-2014 (Annexure-E). On the other hand the Memo dated 12-5-2014 (Annexure-D) has been issued by DSE directing the petitioner to pay the said share transfer fee of Taka 2,40,990. But surprisingly, on the face of the said Memo dated 12-5-2014 as annexed by the petitioner, it appears that the said Memo dated 12-5-2014 has been received by its issuer, i.e. DSE, itself on 19-5-2014. DSE, being the issuer of the Memo dated 12-5-2014, is not supposed to receive its own memo. However, the co-incidence of the date of the receipt of the said memo dated 12-5-2014 by DSE on 19-5-2014 and the date of the pay order dated 19-5-2014 leads to irresistible conclusion that the person who arranged the pay order dated 19-5-2014 had probably submitted the said memo dated 12-5-2014 with DSE. The said Moniruzzaman submitted the said Memo dated 12-5-2014 with DSE again and therefore the petitioner has all the knowledge of the said Memo dated 12-5-2014. Moreover, from the received seal of DSE as engraved on Annexure-C and Annexure-D, it is proved that the copy of the Annexure-C and Annexure-D were not obtained from the respondent No. 2 

 Bank, because respondent No. 2 Bank is not supposed to, and has no reason to submit, the said application for approval dated 7-5-2014 and approval of DSE dated 12-5-2014 with DSE, and hence the petitioner falsely stated in paragraph No. 18 of the said application that the said originals are lying with the respondent No. 2 Bank. The petitioner must have had custody of the originals of the said application for approval dated 7-5-2014 along with the received seal of DSE and the said approval dated 12-5-2014 along with the received seal. Accordingly the petitioner is well aware of the whole share transfer transactions, and the said share transfer has been made by the petitioner himself as well as in the mode and manner the petitioner instructed his employees, namely the said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan and Moniruzzaman; that the petitioner has annexed a letter dated 20-5-2014 issued by Pubali Bank Securities Ltd. addressing the petitioner as Annexure-F. Pursuant to the said letter dated 20-5-2014, a letter dated 29-5-2014 (Annexure-G) was sent to Dhaka Stock Exchange from the end of petitioner. The said letter dated 29-5-2014 (Annexure-G) appears to be received by DSE on 4-6-2014. On 4-6-2014, the respondent No. 1 was not in Bangladesh. Moreover, from the sequence of facts, it is clear that the said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan and Moniruzzaman submitted application for approval dated 7-5-2014, arranged pay order for share transfer fees and therefore the said letter dated 4-6-2014 must have been submitted by the said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan and the said Moniruzzaman at the instruction of the petitioner; that the petitioner in the said application has stated that "as per the Expert Report, the signatures of the petitioner appearing in the DRF Forms, the Gift Application and the Forged Letter "are not independent creations but instead are photocopied from the same source". Crucially, the Export Report does not state who may done such alleged photocopying. It is stated that from the sequence of facts it appears that the petitioner instructed the said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan to complete the transfer of shares from petitioner to the respondent No. 1 and therefore it is proved that if the signatures of the petitioners are at all photocopied from the same source, then the said act must have been done by his employees, namely the said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan and Moniruzzaman at his instruction. Hence, the petitioner cannot challenge the said share transfers when he is involved in the whole transfer process, and on the other hand the respondent No. 1 is fully innocent to this process; that the said 2,77,00,000 shares were transferred from the petitioner to the respondent No. 1 out of 3,45,55,152 shares. After transfer of the said 2,77,00,000 shares, there were remaining 68,55,152 shares in his BO Account. Thereafter, the petitioner received dividends as declared by respondent No. 2 Bank in the year 2015 and 2016. But the petitioner received the said dividends for a particular number of shares which is much lesser than the said shares of 2,77,00,000. The petitioner received the said dividends for a smaller number of shares than his original number of shares without any hue or cry and without raising any objection with anybody or forum. The petitioner received dividend for smaller amount of shares without any demur only because the petitioner himself transferred the said shares in the name of the respondent No. 1 and the petitioner actually informed the respondent No. 1 as to gift of the said shares in her name before and after completion of the transfer. 

 5. The respondent No. 2, the City Bank Limited, has also submitted an affidavit-in-opposition mainly stating that, in compliance of By-law 9.2.1, the petitioner obtained Form-8 (Standard Form prescribed in the By-laws), i.e., Dematerialization Request Form from Pubali Bank Securities Ltd., who is CDBL participant and the petitioner is maintaining his BO Account with this CDBL participant. Thereafter, in compliance of By-law 9.2.1 the said Dematerialization Request Form required the petitioner to state that "the original certificates as listed above are hereby surrendered by me for dematerialization and ", and to submit the original share certificates along the said Dematerialization Request Form. The petitioner submitted all original certificates for dematerialization of 60,46,540 shares with Pubali Bank Securities Ltd. Pubali Bank Securities Ltd. in compliance of By-law 9.2 scrutinized and vetted the said share certificates submitted by the petitioner with it; that thereafter Pubali Bank Securities Ltd. in compliance of By-law 9.2.2 to entered a demat instruction into the system of CDBL, i.e., respondent No. 7, in accordance with user manual (user manual means the user manual framed by CDBL). Thereafter, as provided under By-law 9.2.3, CDBL provided the respondent No. 2 Bank with detailed information of the said Dematerialization Request through system; that after scrutinization of the said share certificates of the petitioner by Pubali Bank Securities Ltd, the petitioner as per By-law 9.2.4 through his employee namely Shamsul Bhuiyan submitted original share certificates along with DRFs and list of share certificates details prepared by Pubali Bank Securities Ltd. enclosed with forwarding letter Nos. 754/14, 755/14, 756/14, 757/14, 758/14, 759/14, 760/14 and 761/14 all dated 4-5-2014, with the respondent No. 2 Bank. The said forwarding letters along with the certificate details prepared by Pubali Bank Securities Ltd., DRFs and share certificates [Annexures-"II", II(A), II(B), II(C), II(D), II(E), II(F) & II(G)]; that the respondent No. 2 Bank, having received the said DRFs, original share certificates (total 154 in number) and forwarding of Pubali Bank Securities Ltd., checked the validity of the share certificates and found that the said share certificates are in the name of the petitioner and request for dematerialization has been made by the petitioner. Accordingly the said share certificates were dematerialized on 5-5-2014; that from the face of the said Dematerialization Request Forms dated 4-5-2014, it appears that the signatures of the petitioner on all DRFs appear to be in blue colour, and the said signature is vetted by Pubali Bank Securities Ltd. In the bare eyes, there is no good reason to doubt the signatures of the petitioner, moreso when the originals of the share certificates have been surrendered. The petitioner for all material times has never informed the respondent No. 2 Bank that the said share certificates referred to in the said DRFs were lost or misplaced. Hence, there is no reason to conclude that the petitioner himself filled in the said DRFs and submitted the same along with the original share certificate through his employee, said Mr Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan. The said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan always contacts with the officials of the bank for and on behalf of the petitioner. Hence, the respondent No. 2 Bank with outmost good faith and bona fide dematerialized the said share certificates; that the Annexure-C is application for approval to the gifting of shares dated 7-5-2014. The deponent of this affidavit can recall that the tadbirkar and employee of the petitioner namely Mr Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan brought the said application for approval to gifting of shares dated 7-5-2014 duly filled in by the petitioner and the deponent on behalf of the respondent No. 2 Bank on bare eyes having found the said signature of the petitioner on the said application for approval not different from the signatures of the petitioner on other documents lying with the respondent No. 2 Bank verified the said signature and signed & sealed the same, and then and there the deponent of this affidavit handed over the said application for approval to the tadbirkar and the employee of the petitioner, namely Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan. The petitioner alleges that the original of the said application for approval dated 7-5-2014 is lying with the respondent No. 2 Bank, which is not true. The respondent No. 2 Bank does not have custody of the original application for approval dated 7-5-2014; that the petitioner also alleges that the originals of Annexures-D, E, F, G, H & I are under custody of the respondent No. 2 Bank, which is not true. The respondent No. 2 Bank does not have custody of any of the said annexures; that the petitioner alleges that the signatures of Annexure-B series, Annexure-C and Annexure-sG are forged by way of scanning or photocopying from the same source. From the record of the respondent No. 2 Bank, it is found that the petitioner vide his letter No. NG/HO/ LETTER/10/2014 dated 10-3-2014 authorized one Mr Ali to collect 6,04,654 shares. Accordingly the said Mr Ali received the said 6, 04,654 number of shares for and on behalf of the petitioner. The signatures of the petitioner on the said letter dated 10-3-2014 matches with all the signatures of Annexures-B series, Annexure-C and Annexure-G. All the signatures of Annexures-B series, Annexure-C and Annexure-G and the signatures of the petitioner on the said letter dated 10-3-2014 are identical. If the signatures of the said Annexure-B Series, Annexure-C and Annexure-G are from same sources, then the signatures on the said letter dated 10-3-2014 must be from exactly same source. The two signatures of the petitioner on the same document, i.e. the said letter dated 10-3-2014 are also identical, and appears to be generated from same source. The petitioner never raised any claim that he did not receive the said 6,04,654 number of shares, neither the petitioner has ever alleged that the said Mr Ali fraudulently or by way of forgery collected the said 6,04,654 number of shares, nor the petitioner ever disowned the said signature of the petitioner on the said letter dated 10-3-2014. Since, the petitioner owns the said signatures of the petitioner on the said letter dated 10-3-2014 and beneficiary of the action of the said letter dated 10-3-2014, the petitioner cannot disown the said signatures on Annexures-B series, Annexure-C and Annexure-G. On the very date of the said letter dated 10-3-2014, i.e., on 10-3-2014 and on 22-4-2014, when the said Mr Ali collected the said 6,04,654 shares, the petitioner as per his own statement was not inside country. Therefore, it is submitted that it appears that the petitioner habitually submits documents in the manner of scanning or photocopying his signatures from same source through his employee namely the said Mr Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan, when he remains outside country. The connection of the said Mr Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan to the said letter dated 10-3-2014 and scanning and copying the signatures of petitioner on other documents comes to surface from another letter being letter No. NG/HO/Letter/CBL/06/2014 dated 2-3-2014 signed by the said Mr Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan for the petitioner. The petitioner vide the said letter dated 2-3-2014 (which is signed by the said Mr Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan) earlier requested the respondent No. 2 Bank to release the said 6,04,654 shares, for which the petitioner submitted the said letter dated 10-3-2014 authorizing one Mr Ali to collect the said 6,04,654 shares. Therefore, it is admitted position that the said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan was directly involved for and on behalf of the petitioner to submit the said documents dated 10-3-2014, 2-3-2014 and the documents in the said Annexures-B series, Annexure-C and Annexure-G. One letter dated 18-2-2004 submitted by the said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan shows that the said Shamsul Alam Bhuiyan is involved with the enterprises of the petitioner long before. Copy of the said letters dated 10-3-2014, 2-3-2014 and 18-2-2004 [Annexures-"III", "III(A)" & "III(B)1"; that the petitioner in his application states that the petitioner from 1-1-2014 to 23-7-2014 was outside Bangladesh. But it appears that the petitioner submitted the said letter dated 10-3-2014 for empowering Mr Haider Ali to collect share certificates. The petitioner again vide his letter dated 7-7-2014 authorized the said Mr Haider Ali for collection of cheque from The City Bank Ltd., which City Bank received on 14-7-2014. Thereafter the petitioner again vide his letter dated 16-7-2014 requested the respondent No. 2 Bank for return of various title deeds and documents. The petitioner does not disowns these letters dated 10-3-2014, 7-7-2014 and 16-7-2014, the signatures of which appears to be identical to each other and also identical to the signatures of Annexures-B series, Annexure-C and Annexure-G, and also appears to be generated from same source. All these relevant time of 10- 3-2014, 11-3-2014 (when the said letter dated 10-3-2014 was received by the respondent No. 2 Bank, 7-7-2014, 14-7-2014 (when the City Bank received the said letter dated 7-7-2014) and 16-7-2014, the petitioner was not as per his own statement inside Bangladesh. Since the petitioner does not disowns these letters and was direct beneficiary of these letters, it appears that the petitioner is habitual in submitting letters through his employees while he is outside Bangladesh by way of copying signatures from an identical source. Copy of the said letters dated 7-7-2014 and 16-7-2014 [Annexure-"IV" & "IV(A)"]; that the petitioner on 17-9-2014 vide his letter dated 16-9-2014 again authorized the said Mr Haider Ali to collect certain documents from the respondent No. 2 Bank. This letter date 16-9-2014 of the petitioner, it appears that the said Mr Haider Ali is connected to the petitioner and the petitioner had knowledge of the earlier letters dated 10-3-2014 and 7-7-2014 under which the said Mr Haider Ali was empowered to collect documents. Copy of the said letter dated 16-9-2014 (Annexure-"V"); that the petitioner is used to filing letters with the respondent No. 2 Banks, which is proved from his letter date 11-1-2014 as well. The petitioner submitted his letter dated 11-1-2014 with the respondent No. 2 Bank, which the respondent No. 2 Bank received on 22-1-2014, and the petitioner, as per his statement, was outside Bangladesh at the relevant time of 11-1-2014 and 22-1-2014. The petitioner vide the said letter dated 11-1-2014 requested the respondent No. 2 Bank to transmit certain shares of his late father to his name (Annexure-VI). 

 7. Learned Advocate Mr Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh, appearing for the petitioner and having placed the petition, submits that the title as regards 2,77,00,000 (two crore seventy seven lac) number of shares is in dispute in this case. He next submits that, the petitioner holds 3,45,55,152 numbers of shares in the Lity tunic Limited (CBL), but the petitioner had left Bangladesh on 3-1-2014 for treatment and returned to Bangladesh on 23-7-2014, vide the entries, made by the Bangladesh and the UK authorities on his Passport No. E 1221750, annexed to the petition as Annexure-H. As such, in between 4-1-2014 to 23-7-2014, the petitioner was not in Bangladesh. He proceeds on that, during the absence of the petitioner a number of total 2,77,00,000 (two crore seventy seven lac) shares were shown to have been transferred, in favour of respondent No. 1, by forging his signature in the 'application for approval to the gifting of shares, dated 7-5-2014 in Form III(A), annexed as Annexure-C. The learned Advocate then referred to the specific case of the petitioner as stated in paragraph No. 9 of the petition. He further submits that the petitioner was not in Bangladesh during May, 2014, and he had never signed the Dematerialization Request Form (DRF) or the application for approval to the gifting of share dated 7-5-2014 (Annexure-C), nor he has received the letter of DSE approval dated 12-5-2014 (Annexure-D). He continues that the petitioner did not receive the letter dated 20-5-2014 of the PBSL (Annexure-F) regarding change of ownership of his shares, nor be had written the letter dated 29-5-2014 (Annexure-G) to the DSE intimating the alleged transfer of his shares. The learned Advocate also points out that the petitioner never received the letter dated 14-7-2015, addressed to the Respondent No. 1 (Annexure-J) or a certificate under reference No. ho.sd.2015/711 dated 14-10-2014 (Annexure: J-1) of CBL confirming issuance of bonus shares or stock dividend, since that was received by the Respondent No.1. So, he had no knowledge of any of these letters. The learned Advocate asserts that the petitioner had never executed any deed of gift, nor there is any case of making deed of gift of 2,77,00,000 number of shares. The learned Advocate emphatically argues that all these documents and letters were created and signed in May, 2014 when the petitioner was staying in England and as such, he did neither signed therein, nor he was in Bangladesh at the relevant time to sign any of them, nor had he received any of them, nor had he any knowledge of them. The further case of the petitioner is that, he did never instruct anybody to put his signature on any of those papers. Even, the learned Advocate emphasises that, there is no case stated by the respondent No. 1, or by any other respondent that, the petitioner had informed the bank that he has gifted the shares to the respondent No. 1 or that he had instructed the bank to process the gift. Even the bank had never asked the petitioner as to whether he had gifted these huge amounts of shares to the Respondent No. 1 or if he (petitioner) had signed the Form III(A) dated 7-5-2014 (Annexure-C). The learned Advocate proceeds on that the petitioner was not even aware of the Pay Order No. 1527025 dated 19-5-2014 of Bank Asia, issued in his absence for payment of Taka 2,40,990 to Dhaka Stock Exchange Limited, as transfer fees, which is required to be paid to give effect to such transfer by way of gift. He continues that the petitioner had no knowledge, nor he gave any instruction on 20-5-2014 for payment of transfer fees (service charge) as claimed by the respondent No. 1. Rather, in the course of the further hearing, the learned Advocate Mr Mohammad Mehedi Hasan Chowdhury, referring to an office note dated 21-5-2014 of Nurani Group (Annexure: 2 to the affidavit in opposition of respondent No. 1), submits that in this office note it has been recorded that, upon an instruction of the Managing Director of Noorani Group (the petitioner), given over telephone on 20-5-2014, the transfer fees for transferring 2,77,00,000 number of City Bank's share in the name of Deputy Managing Director Madam (respondent No. 1) was paid. Therefore, the learned Advocate points out that, the pay order by which the said transfer fees has been paid as service charge is dated 19-5-2014, vide the Pay Order dated 19-5-2015 (Annexure-E), whereas this note has been initiated on 21-5-2014. If this story were true then the Pay Order should have been issued on 21-5-2014 or on a following dated, he hastens to add. Therefore, he asserts, that this note sheet belies the entire story of the respondent No. 1, from the very inception, that the petitioner had given instruction on 20-5-2014, over phone, to pay service charge to the Dhaka Stock Exchange Limited (DSE), or that he had any intention to make gift of the aforesaid shares to the respondent No. 1. In these circumstances, he proceeds on that, the petitioner procured all the questioned documents, have got the same for examination by an expert, who has, after examining the same, expressed his opinion on 18-7-2016, in a letter addressed to the petitioner (Annexure-I), in which the expert has stated that the signature on the questioned documents, including the application for approval for gifting the shares (Annexure-C), were very identical and that putting such identical signatures on several documents was not possible in the normal course of writing or signing and that these signatures, purported to be that of the petitioner, were put directly or indirectly through cutting and pasting or by photocopying or scanning (i.e. mechanically transferred from one to another). The learned Advocate maintains that, if the petitioner had intended to make gift of these shares to the respondent No. 1, then the service charge would have been paid at his instruction from his own account, instead of account of Noorani Group. But, that is not the case. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further asserts that, the petitioner is not at all aware of the daily balance dated 6-6-2014, in which the number of shares held by the petitioner in the account of CDBL has been shown (Annexure-A), nor about the DRF Form (Annexure-B series) and that the petitioner had neither put his signature on those documents, nor was aware about these documents. Hence, the learned Advocate sums up that, the respondent No. 1 has acquired no right or title in the disputed shares or in the bonus shares issued against the said shares and that name of the petitioner may be entered in the Register of shares of the CBL and that of the Respondent No. 1 be deleted from the register of the bank and in the CDBL account, by rectifying the same. 

 9. Mr Mustafizur Rahman Khan, learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1, submits that by a letter dated 12-5-2014, the petitioner was asked by the DSE to deposit the service charge in favour of the DSE for transferring 2,77,00,000 (two crore seventy seven lac) shares of CBL in favour of his spouse, the respondent No. 1, by way of gift. The further case of the respondent No. 1 is that, she was also in London as the transferor was, when the transfer was given effect to. But, the circumstance and the uninterrupted sequence of the events, clearly prove that the gift of these shares, to the Respondent No. 1, were done in the manner as designed by the petitioner himself. The learned Advocate then adds to his submissions that this gift was done voluntarily and through a process by which the petitioner does habitually deal with his shares in the CBL. Therefore, he concludes that, this is a clear case of making voluntary gift of 2,77,00,000 number shares of CBL in favour of the respondent No. 1 by the petitioner and that this petition has no merit and the same is liable to be dismissed. 

 10. Mr Ahsanul Karim, and Mr Khairul Alam Chowdhury, Advocates, have appeared on behalf of the respondent No. 2 Bank (the CBL). Mr Ahsanul Karim submits that the petitioner got 60,46,540 number of shares dematerialized through PBSL and on his behalf one Shamsul Islam Bhuiyan had dealt with the bank. He further submits that the petitioner is used to deal with his shares through his employees and, he specifically submits, that, one M.  11. This matter has appeared in the cause list on 9-7-2017 for further hearing. The learned Advocate Mr Mohammad Mehedi Hasan Chowdhury, for the petitioner, having placed an affidavit-in-reply, dated 6-7-2017 (submitted on 9-7-2017), filed on behalf of the petitioner, refers to some notes of approval of Noorani Group, respectively dated 4-1-2014 (Annexure-N), dated 19-4-2014 (Annexure:N-1), dated 4-4-2014 (Annexure: N-3), salary increment statement (Annexure-O), and another note of approval dated 19-5-2014 and then submits that these and other documents annexed to this reply would show that the DMD (Respondent No. 1) and the CEO have been independently running and managing the affairs of the Noorani Group by giving necessary instructions and approvals and even by approving cost and expenses. Therefore, he emphasis that, clearly the employees who are said to be dealing with the CBL were all acting under the instruction and direction of the DMD (Respondent No. 1), not under the Managing Director (petitioner), who was then staying in London for treatment. He further submits that in paragraph No. 16 of the bank's affidavit-in-opposition, it has been admitted that, the petitioner habitually submits documents by scanning or photocopying from the same source through his employee, the said M. Shamsul Alam Bahiyan, when he remains out of the country. He therefore emphatically argues that, as admitted by the Bank, the petitioner himself did not put his signature on Form III(A), and that the signatures appearing on the DRF and other letters including the application dated 7-5-2014 for approval to gifting shares (Annexure-C) were put by scanning during his (petitioner's) absence. Therefore, the learned Advocate was very serious in urging upon the Court to take legal action against the concerned officials of the bank alleging that the bank has acted without exercising due diligence and had verified the signature of the petitioner though it was not original according to their knowledge and the so-called verification of a signature on Form No. III(A) was done even without making any query with the petitioner, though it involved a huge number of shares. Appeared at this stage, as Senior Advocate for the petitioner, Mr Akhtar Imam continued the submission, with leave of the Court, that once the petitioner has denied his signature, on the application, dated 7-5-2014, for approval of gifting shares in Form III(A) to the petition (Annexure-C), then the burden of proof shifts and lies upon the Respondent No. 1 to prove that the petitioner had in fact made a gift of the disputed shares in her favour and that the signature appearing on Form III(A) for approval of the gift is the signature of the petitioner. He has relied upon an unreported judgment, passed in Civil Revision No. 1443 of 2008, wherein in a case concerning a dispute regarding payment of rent between the landlord and the tenant, if has been held that, once the landlord has denied to have received the rent, the duty to prove payment of the rent has been shifted to the other side i.e. upon the tenant. Learned Advocate Mr Kazi Akter Hamid, also in the relay, at the last stage, stood for the petitioner. He submits that the process of gift of the disputed shares has not been done in accordance with law and if the petitioner had any intention to make a gift of his shares then he would have ratified all these acts in writing or otherwise, but there is no such proof that the petitioner had even ratified or intended to ratify the disputed transfer by way of gift, while his clear case is that he did not make any gift of his shares to Respondent No. 1. 

 15. Regulation 42(1) of the DSE Listing Regulation, reads as follows: "42.(1)All shares of public companies listed with the exchange shall be sold through the trading system of exchange. (2) Where ,—(a) transfer of the share is to be made by the registered shareholder to his close relative (i.e. spouse, son, daughter, father, mother, brother or sister) by way of gift, the transferor shall apply to the exchange; in Form III(A) for prior approval to effect such transfer or transaction. Besides, service charge to the extent of Taka 0.05% on the closing paragraph of the scrip shall be payable to the exchange for each transfer, vide proviso to Regulation No. 42. 

 16. Therefore, as required by sub-regulation (2) of Regulation No. 42 of the DSE Listing Regulation, for transferring shares of the CBL (a public company) listed with the DSE, by way of gift, prior approval of the DSE shall have to be obtained by submitting an application for approval of gifting the shares in Form III(A), appended to the Regulations and to be submitted being accompanied by the documents as mentioned in the said form and the service charge for such transfer shall have to be paid to the DSE, to legally give effect to any transfer of listed security by way of gift. The provisions of Regulation 42 read with section 31 of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 shall prevail over section 38 of the Companies Act, 1994. Indeed, after obtaining the approval of gift, from the DSE, a gift will have to be made and proved, in any legally admissible from, since the approval for making gift' will require an act of gift to be done following such approval, unless such approval is given post-facto upon a gift made beforehand. But, there is no materials or evidence on record that, any such gift was at all made. 

 18. It appears that the respondent No. 1 claims to have derived title by way of gift of these 2,77,00,000 shares based on the approval of the DSE, given upon an application for approval of gifting shares, submitted in a Form III(A) dated 7-5-2014 (Annexure-C). This Form III(A) dated 7-5-2014, in which the application for DSE approval has been made is a Form that was appended to the DSE Listing Regulation published on 8-4-1996. No documents were then required to be enclosed while submitting an application in the old Form III(A), prescribed on 8-4-1996. But, this Form III(A) has been modified on 8-8-010, vide the Gazette notification published on 30-9-2010, by the DSE. 

 19. Form III(A), modified on 8-8-2010, requires some documents to be enclosed with the "application for approval to the gifting of shares", that includes, amongst other, the National Identification Card (NID)/Passport of both transferor and transferee. But, the application dated 7-5-2014, submitted to the DSE for approval of the gifting shares (i.e. for approval of a transfer beyond the trading system of the exchange) was neither made in the proper form, as prescribed/modified on 30-9-2010, nor the documents required to been enclosed therewith, were indeed enclosed for consideration of granting the approval by the DSE. This Form 111(A) has been modified on 8-8-2010. (vide Gazette Notification dated 30-9-2010) by the DSE in exercise of the power vested in it by section 34(1) of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969. This modification of Form III(A) is not a mere expression of artistic choice, but a legal instrument to be mandatorily used for submitting any application for approval to gifting the shares of a company listed with the Exchange. Hence, for not submitting the application dated 7-5-2014 (Annexure-I) in the proper form, prescribed by law, the said application dated 7-5-2014 was not an application in the eye of law and the DSE had no authority to consider or to grant any approval on the same. Hence, in my considered opinion, the approval of DSE, even if, everything were genuine, is not an approval in the eye of law, therefore, the same is ultra-vires and ineffective. It cannot and does not legally transfer to respondent No. 1 any title in the disputed shares. 

 20. Besides, since the petitioner and the Respondent No. 1, both were in London on 7-5-2014, therefore it was not possible to enclose his or her NID/or passport with this application dated 7-5-2014 (Annexure-C). Hence, also the said application was not proper, since it was not submitted by enclosing legally required documents. The another aspect of it is that, if there was an intention on the part of the petitioner to make gift, then the applicant-petitioner should have submitted the application dated 7-5-2014 (Annexure-C) alongwith the legally required documents for approval of gift. The petitioner or the DSE cannot waive these statutory requirement. 

 21. Then, I have examined a note of approval dated 19-5-2014 (Annexure-T), that reads as follows: 

 Note for approval "2,22,00,000 number of shares of The City Bank Limited to be transferred from Mr AKM Zakaria Hossain Choudhury to Ms. Sabrina Choudhury as gift. As such an amount of Taka 6,50,000 (Taka six lac fifty thousand) only will be required for miscellaneous purpose. A copy of FORM III(A), Regulation-42) for transferring the same and deposited to Dhaka Stock Exchange Limited on 8-5-2014. As per instruction of DMD Madam the  above mentioned fund would be provided from Noorani Centre fund Submitted for kind information and approval please. 

 25. It is also to be noted here that, the question of apparent similarity between the signatures appearing on the DRF and on Form III(A) is not the issue in this case. The issue is, whether the petitioner himself had put any signature on the Form No. III(A) dated 7-5-2014 (Annexure-C), which is a legally mandatory requirement for making a gift of the shares of a public company listed with the exchange. Even the theory that the petitioner usually deals with his shares through a scanning his signature will, in no way, help improving the case of the respondent No. 1, because the request for approval of the gift of share must be based and considered on the original signature of the petitioner, to be put on Form III(A), and nothing less then that can constitute any valid gift or confer any valid title in the disputed shares, moreso, in the absence of any proof of gift, as distinct from unapproval for gift. Any deviation from this will no; only be illegal, rather it will open a floodgate for doing fraud and forgery in the hands of unscrupulous officials or persons at various level. 

 26. Therefore, these factual issues, based on the preponderance of the evidence, clearly prove that the petitioner himself did not sign the application dated 7-5-2014 (Annexure-C) in Form III(A) for approval of gifting his 2,77,00,000 shares, nor he had taken any decision to pay service charge on 19-5-2014 for transferring the disputed shares was taken by him, nor he had any intention to make the questioned gift, nor was it possible on his part to do the alleged act, done during his absence from 4-1-2014 to 23-7-2014. In consequence, the burden to prove that the petitioner had gifted the shares and other relevant facts, that has been shifted to and rested upon the respondent No. 1, could not be discharged by her. Even, as per section 103 of the Evidence Act, 1872, the burden that rests upon the Respondent No. 1, she has failed to discharge that as well.
